question:
Part of an “\(n\)-pointed regular star” is shown. It is a simple closed polygon in which all \(2n\) edges are congruent, angles \(A_1,\) \(A_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(A_n\) are congruent, and angles \(B_1,\) \(B_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(B_n\) are congruent. If the acute angle at \(A_1\) is \(10^\circ\) less than the acute angle at \(B_1,\) then \(n=\)

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_12_Q20_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The important distinction is that the acute angle at an inward vertex \(B_i\) lies outside the star. Its polygon interior angle is the remaining reflex angle.

Let \(\alpha\) be the acute angle at each outward vertex \(A_i\), and let \(\beta\) be the acute angle at each inward vertex \(B_i\). The given condition is \(\beta-\alpha=10^\circ\). The polygon's interior angles are therefore \(\alpha\) at each \(A_i\) and \(360^\circ-\beta\) at each \(B_i\).

There are \(n\) vertices of each kind, giving \(2n\) vertices altogether. The interior-angle sum formula applies to this simple polygon even though it is concave, so
\[
n\bigl(\alpha+360^\circ-\beta\bigr)
=(2n-2)180^\circ.
\]
Substituting \(\beta-\alpha=10^\circ\) gives
\[
350n=360n-360,
\qquad 10n=360.
\]
Hence \(n=\boxed{36}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
